artifact: BEYU OS 2.0 Production Readiness Evidence Matrix
environment: Disposable CI-equivalent: PostgreSQL 16.14 embedded cluster, Node 22.22.3, 2 vCPU / 4 GB sandbox, no production credentials, no cloud infrastructure.
evidence_integrity_policy: Every item names the exact command that reproduces it. Nothing here is asserted on the basis of documentation. Evidence marked ENVIRONMENT_LIMITED failed only because this sandbox lacks production access; it is not evidence of product failure.

evidence.claim: The baseline builds, typechecks, lints and contains no committed secrets.
evidence.test: npx tsc --noEmit; npm run lint; npm run build; node scripts/scan-secrets.mjs
evidence.result: tsc exit 0; eslint exit 0 over 256 root TS files; next build exit 0 (65 route entries, 45 under /api/*, 5 pages prerendered); scan-secrets 'Scan complete: 1180 files scanned, no potential secrets found.'
evidence.risk: None.

evidence.claim: Agriculture OS has no implementation, while the control plane declares authority for it.
evidence.test: ls sectors/ ; find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -iname '*agriculture*' -print ; find src/app/api -name route.ts
evidence.result: sectors/ contains only 'health'. No agriculture backend, tables, or migrations. 45 API routes exist; 0 match /api/v1/agriculture/*. Flutter mobile maps the sector to a 'FUTURE / NOT YET INTEGRATED' placeholder.
evidence.risk: os_registry row AGRICULTURE_OS = ACTIVE with dataAuthority [FARM_BLOCK, CROP_CYCLE, HARVEST] and apis ['/api/v1/agriculture/*']; 54 tracked files with 141 occurrences.

evidence.claim: The declared Agriculture data authority is not backed by any table.
evidence.test: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ... WHERE relname LIKE '%farm%' OR '%crop%' OR '%harvest%' OR '%agri%'
evidence.result: 0 rows. 118 total tables exist; none agriculture-related.
evidence.risk: A declared-but-absent data domain cannot be isolated, audited or restored.

evidence.claim: All 28 root migrations apply from an empty database, re-running changes nothing, and the migration set matches the schema (no drift).
evidence.test: npx tsx scripts/migrate.ts; npx tsx scripts/migrate.ts; npx drizzle-kit generate --name=drift_check; git status --short drizzle/
evidence.result: Run 1: '28 total / 28 APPLIED', fingerprint 8a5acf4ba4b69d57737e6f90c90053a5. Run 2: '0 total ... 28 APPLIED', identical fingerprint (no-op). drizzle-kit generate: 'No config changes detected' and wrote no file; git status for drizzle/ empty.
evidence.risk: None locally; production remains blocked (EV-020).

evidence.claim: Tenant, entity and global scopes are enforced by PostgreSQL for the runtime role, including when the application forgets to filter.
evidence.test: npx vitest run tests/security/rls-isolation.test.ts
evidence.result: 13/13 pass against live PostgreSQL as beyu_runtime: cross-tenant SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE denied; zero-scope GUC denied; unqualified UPDATE denied; scope-array manipulation (extra element, tenant id swap) denied; forged GUC through request body yields the same denial; defence-in-depth case drops the tenant WHERE clause entirely and still cannot leak.
evidence.risk: Covers 1 of 118 tables; 34 tenant-scoped tables have no RLS backstop (EV-007).

evidence.claim: The application connects as a non-privileged role and this is now asserted at runtime.
evidence.test: npx tsx scripts/setup-db-role.ts; curl -H "cookie: $SESSION" /api/v1/system/self-test; npx vitest run tests/security/runtime-privilege-guard.test.ts
evidence.result: rolesuper=f, rolbypassrls=f, rolcreaterole=f, rolcreatedb=f for beyu_runtime. CTL-SEC-011 returns passed:true with detail 'role "beyu_runtime" is suitably unprivileged (NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS, NOCREATEROLE, NOCREATEDB)'. New guard test asserts non-vacuity: with a privileged DSN it must return ok=false.
evidence.risk: Previously NO production code path asserted this; a misconfigured production DSN would have silently unbound RLS. Closed by this program.

evidence.claim: Ten governed tables are RLS-enabled without FORCE, and 34 tenant-scoped tables have no RLS; isolation for those rests on application filters.
evidence.test: SELECT relname, relrowsecurity, relforcerowsecurity FROM pg_class ...; rg -o "from\(([a-zA-Z_]+)\)"
evidence.result: 118 tables / 44 RLS / 34 FORCE / 44 policies. 10 enable-only: approvals, enterprise_memory, internal_event_receipts, knowledge_sources, noelia_action_requests, noelia_schedules, noelia_schedule_runs, noelia_scheduler_offsets, noelia_workflow_steps, noelia_workflows. 34 tables have tenant_id/entity_id/country_code but no RLS; 14 of those have no read path in src/. Live reads on the other 20 always apply inArray(table.tenantId, scope). The non-RLS decision in 0014_scope_tenant_id.sql is documented and deliberate (owner-grantor bypass, append-only tables, no migration GRANT).
evidence.risk: A future missing WHERE clause leaks across tenants with no database backstop and no failing test.

evidence.claim: Audit and enterprise-event chains are append-only, tamper-evident, and survive concurrent writers.
evidence.artifact: chain integrity tests + live ledger verification + DR drill
evidence.test: npx vitest run tests/database/atomic-audit.test.ts tests/certification/scale-concurrency.test.ts tests/internal/events-internal.test.ts; npx tsx scripts/dr-drill.ts
evidence.result: 1000 concurrent audit inserts + 200 concurrent event ingests: chains verified by hash recomputation, no gaps or forks. API-level HMAC chain verified for 3 entries with independent recomputation. Cross-OS test proves a malformed event leaves zero audit trail, a replay is DENIED while the original audit survives, and forged traces are rejected. DR drill confirms 'audit chain remains intact' and 'enterprise event chain remains intact' on the restored copy. Live ledger: audit_log=2, internal_event_receipts=2.
evidence.risk: None identified.

evidence.claim: The full root regression suite passes with zero failures and zero skips on live PostgreSQL, before and after this program's changes.
evidence.test: npx vitest run --reporter=json
evidence.result: Baseline: 123 files / 2451 tests passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped in 354.89s. Post-change: 125 files / 2466 tests passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped in 418.12s (+2 files, +15 tests, all passing).
evidence.risk: None.

evidence.claim: Health OS migrations and its PostgreSQL security layers are real, applied and passing.
evidence.artifact: npm run migration:identity:up + jest security subset
evidence.test: cd sectors/health/backend && npm run migration:identity:up && node --experimental-vm-modules ./node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js --runInBand src/security src/database src/identity
evidence.result: 30/30 migrations (006..030) applied to a real PostgreSQL 16 database beyu_health. Security subset: 10 suites / 94 tests pass, including isolation-boundaries, rls-enforcement, security-rls, security-audit-chain, security-config-hardening.
evidence.risk: None for the tested surface.

evidence.claim: The whole Health backend suite passes.
evidence.artifact: jest full run + bounded remainder batch
evidence.test: node --experimental-vm-modules ./node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js --runInBand --ci --forceExit
evidence.result: 93 suites total: 62 passed in the first full run (process then OOM-killed by the 4 GB sandbox), the remaining 31 in a bounded batch (29 passed, 2 env-gated skips). Both skips then passed once the live root federation environment was supplied (EV-013, EV-014). Net: 93/93 PASS, 0 failures.
evidence.risk: The single-run OOM is an environment limit of this sandbox, not a Health OS defect; recorded as such.
evidence.environment_note: ENVIRONMENT_LIMITED: cannot run all 93 PGlite suites concurrently on 4 GB; must be run in batches here.

evidence.claim: Health frontend and backend static gates pass, and the CI lint annotation is stale.
evidence.test: cd sectors/health/frontend && npm run typecheck && npm run build && npx vitest run ; cd ../backend && ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false ./node_modules/.bin/eslint -f json 'src/**/*.ts'
evidence.result: Frontend: `npm run typecheck` exit 0, `npm run build` (Vite 7.3.2) exit 0 — `dist/index.html` 1,035.89 kB / gzip 263.75 kB via `vite-plugin-singlefile`, vitest 3 files / 14 tests pass. Backend lint: 271 files linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings. CI run 34026282329 on main shows the Health backend job success. The inline comment claiming '2522 errors' and 'The job FAILS on this step' describes a state that no longer exists and has been corrected in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
evidence.risk: A stale 'expected failure' annotation invites future engineers to treat a red lint step as normal.

evidence.claim: GlobalUserID identity federation works for real over HTTP between Health OS and the BEYU OS control plane, with revocation.
evidence.test: cd sectors/health/backend && BEYU_OS_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3100 BEYU_INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN=*** TEST_DATABASE_URL=<health> BEYU_OS_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL=<root> node --experimental-vm-modules ./node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js --runInBand cross-os-identity-certification
evidence.result: 10/10 scenarios pass against both live systems: canonical provisioning + sector link; login through live federation with sector-user JWT subject; /auth/me canonical revalidation on cache miss and TTL hit; patient role may read but not register patients; cross-OS SERVICE token cannot impersonate a human Bearer; suspended service principal cannot log in; canonical revocation propagates within the status TTL; restore resumes access; a security_version bump rejects the stale token immediately; the root immutable audit ledger recorded the cross-OS service calls.
evidence.risk: None identified.

evidence.claim: The governed cross-OS event transport (Health billing -> BEYU enterprise event) is exactly-once and reconciles.
evidence.test: cd sectors/health/backend && BEYU_EVENTS_INTEGRATION=1 BEYU_OS_TEST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3100 BEYU_OS_TEST_SERVICE_TOKEN=*** node --experimental-vm-modules ./node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js --runInBand events.integration
evidence.result: 5/5 pass: billing transaction atomically stages the governed event in the outbox; dispatcher delivers to the live root and BEYU records the governed enterprise event; simulated crash-redelivery stays EXACTLY-ONCE at the business level; payment events flow through the same chain; reconciliation reports outbox <-> BEYU receipts consistent.
evidence.risk: None identified.

evidence.claim: Financial ledger integrity is mathematically sound and money is never stored in floating-point columns; posting authority remains governed off.
evidence.artifact: information_schema query + live registry query + finance tests
evidence.test: SELECT table_name,column_name,data_type FROM columns WHERE data_type IN ('float','double precision','real'); SELECT capability_id,status,implementation_status FROM governance_capability_registry; npx vitest run tests/finance
evidence.result: 0 float/real/numeric(18,4) columns: all money is numeric(18,2); journal_lines.debit/credit numeric(20,2); posting requires Number.isSafeInteger and rejects amounts at or beyond 2^53. Registry: 60 capabilities, ALL status=LOCKED, ALL implementation_status=NOT_IMPLEMENTED; journal_entries = 0 rows. tests/finance: ledger-integrity 18, capital-governance 26, ledger-write-authority 6, waterfall 28, tax 19, financial-data-integrity 14, dual-control 4, approval-quorum 7, period-lock 6, reporting-package 7, capital-structure 14, group-consolidation 13 -- all pass.
evidence.risk: GATE 10 is satisfied for the mechanism; the ledger is not operational for real entities because governance has not activated CAP_POSTING. That is the intended state, not a defect.

evidence.claim: The float-based waterfall engine in the production path produces no divergence versus the deterministic BigInt engine, and cannot touch the ledger.
evidence.test: node --test a temporary differential harness (not committed)
evidence.result: 63 cases (20 randomized 4-tier, 20 randomized 3-tier, 9 boundary, 6 randomized 5-tier): 0 divergences in total distributions; float totals are exactly integer-valued and far inside 2^53; deterministic v2 rejects 3 deliberately malformed cases that the loose input normalizer accepted. Source review: waterfallEngine is called from 0 production files; the v1 path uses its own private toCents() and never calls safeMinorUnits(), and never writes journal_entries.
evidence.risk: Latent, not active: v1 would silently floor a fractional-cent input that v2 rejects; the loose normalizer can produce a wrong answer instead of a validation error.

evidence.claim: AI governance holds: kill switch first, human approval, and no real generative inference is possible.
evidence.artifact: assurance control + source trace + provider tests
evidence.test: curl /api/system/self-test; rg OpenAICompatibleAdapter; npx vitest run tests/noelia tests/assurance
evidence.result: ctlNoeliaKillSwitch passed:true 'Kill switch enforced first in route()'; ASSURANCE-003 passed:true; ASSURANCE-006 previously passed on environment variables alone while OpenAICompatibleAdapter was referenced in 0 non-test files. Approval gates, human oversight, and routing determinism tests pass; approval_records and human_review_queue are FORCE RLS. 38 noelia_* tables exist.
evidence.risk: REAL_GENERATIVE_INFERENCE = BLOCKED, and the availability report was not trustworthy in the permissive direction. Fixed by EV-018.

evidence.claim: Generative-inference availability is now derived from what is actually mounted, not from an environment variable alone.
evidence.test: npx vitest run tests/noelia/generative-inference-status.test.ts; npm run build; curl /api/system/self-test
evidence.result: 9/9 new tests pass. The resolver accepts both historical variable names; availability is now 'configured AND mounted', so resilience.ts no longer reports 'OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_ADAPTER_IMPLEMENTED' on env alone; ASSURANCE-006 now FAILS with 'the OpenAI-compatible adapter is not mounted in the gateway's default provider list' instead of silently passing. Both names are documented in .env.example. tsc, eslint, next build all exit 0.
evidence.risk: None; the change makes an existing gap visible rather than closing the gap itself.

evidence.claim: Retrieval-augmented generation is lexical and OS-agnostic; the architecture document's self-declared status is accurate.
evidence.artifact: pg_extension / column inspection + retrieval source review
evidence.test: SELECT extname FROM pg_extension; SELECT count(*) FROM pg_attribute WHERE atttypid='vector'::regtype; review src/lib/noelia/knowledge-fabric.ts retrieve() and memory.ts termsFor()
evidence.result: Extensions: plpgsql, btree_gist only. 0 vector columns; embedding_status/model_id/dimensions exist but are placeholders defaulting to NOT_EMBEDDED. Retrieval is regex tokenisation (<=8 alnum terms) with bound parameters and tenant/entity/country predicates, but no os_id predicate. The audit event records osId without filtering on it. docs/audit/NOELIA_RAG_ARCHITECTURE.md:3 states 'IMPLEMENTED (governed retrieval) + BLOCKED (semantic/embedding runtime)' -- confirmed accurate.
evidence.risk: No semantic search capability exists despite the architecture naming; cross-OS knowledge isolation is not enforced.

evidence.claim: The production database release pipeline cannot run; CI fails closed by design.
evidence.test: gh run list --workflow=db-release.yml; gh run view 34026282327 --log
evidence.result: On main: 'BEYU OS - database release (GitHub -> Supabase)' failure (6m25s). 'Preflight: no mutation, no secret value' failed at ci.yml:149 with EXTERNAL_BLOCKED -- repository secret BEYU_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL is not configured, 'the owner must configure it; the workflow deliberately does not invent a target or a credential.' Migration validation (scratch PostgreSQL 16) success. Production drift check, deploy+verify and runtime verification all skipped by design. gh api .../actions/secrets returned 403 Resource not accessible by integration, so presence cannot be confirmed directly -- inferred from the pipeline's own fail-closed result.
evidence.risk: The Vercel application is deployed to Production (deployment state=success for 0eaa71de) while the schema pipeline is blocked: the app version and the database version are not governed by one release record.
evidence.environment_note: ENVIRONMENT_LIMITED: production secrets are owner-controlled by design; this program must not and cannot supply them.

evidence.claim: A backup/restore drill succeeds and preserves security state.
evidence.test: npx tsx scripts/dr-drill.ts
evidence.result: PASSED. Schema reconstructed from migrations alone (fingerprint parity); 117 tables restored with count parity; RLS set preserved (44 tables); audit chain and enterprise event chain remain intact; 2 audit heads; 5 service principals; scratch database destroyed afterwards.
evidence.risk: Logical/metadata restore only. No managed PITR, no real backup file, no timed restore.
evidence.environment_note: ENVIRONMENT_LIMITED: production RPO/RTO cannot be measured here. No RPO/RTO figures are asserted anywhere in this program.

evidence.claim: Production dependency posture is acceptable at the CI gate, with named residual risk.
evidence.test: npm audit --omit=dev (root); sectors/health/frontend; sectors/health/backend
evidence.result: Root: 0 vulnerabilities. Health frontend: 0. Health backend: 13 moderate, 0 high, 0 critical -- all the transitive 'uuid' DoS advisory via bull, and next via @nestjs/next-shims. CI gate is --audit-level=critical, so all three jobs pass. No high or critical in any production manifest.
evidence.risk: npm audit cannot see end-of-life: @apollo/server ^4.11.0 is a DIRECT production dependency of Health backend and is the live GraphQL driver (app.module.ts), while Apollo Server v4 reached end of support in January 2026.

evidence.claim: SQL injection and stored-privilege review of the whole data layer.
evidence.test: rg 'await sql`' src --count-matches; rg 'sql\.raw|db\.execute\(\s*\x60' src; SELECT routines FROM information_schema WHERE security_type='DEFINER'
evidence.result: Root: 69 sql`` sites across 15 files; every interpolation is a parameterised ${} binding inside a Drizzle SQL object, an operator symbol, or a schema-generated identifier; 0 sql.raw / db.execute / string-concatenated SQL; 0 SECURITY DEFINER functions. Health: 6 routines, all SECURITY DEFINER, all with search_path pinned to pg_catalog,pg_temp, with 29 search_path usages overall.
evidence.risk: None.

evidence.claim: Authentication boundaries are enforced: 401 without credentials, 403 without scope, 429 on rate limit, DENIED audited.
evidence.test: curl /api/v1/health; npx vitest run tests/governance/authorization-http.test.ts
evidence.result: Live: /api/system/self-test -> 401 'Authentication required'; no cookie -> 401. Suite: 14 tests incl. internal 401 without token, 429 after exceeding the limit, 403 for missing scope, scope granted by role, and 'DENIED authorisation decision audited' plus 'denied decision visible in audit trail' all pass.
evidence.risk: Per-principal limiter (120/60s) throttles heavily repeated automated logins; this slows test suites but is deliberate.

evidence.claim: The running control plane is healthy as the runtime role, and the production endpoint could not be verified from this sandbox.
evidence.test: curl /api/health; curl -u ... /api/system/self-test; curl https://beyu-os-1-0.vercel.app/api/health
evidence.result: Local: database:UP with postgres '16.14 (embedded ...)'. Self-test: 12 controls, status HEALTHY, 0 failed, 0 warnings, 0 not_assessed, all areas ACCESS/SECURITY/DATA/INTEGRATION. Production probe: could not complete TLS to beyu-os-1-0.vercel.app (curl exit 35 SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL) while api.github.com returned HTTP 200 from the same sandbox; getent resolved two addresses. Conclusion recorded as unverified, not as down.
evidence.risk: Production behaviour is unverified by this program.

evidence.claim: Operational and incident-management readiness is materially incomplete.
evidence.test: ls docs/runbooks; ls docs/compliance; SELECT relname FROM pg_class WHERE relname LIKE '%incident%'
evidence.result: docs/runbooks contains 2 files (README.md, supabase-production-database.md) against the ~20 runbooks required by the programme. docs/compliance contains only README.md. The only incident table at the control plane is noelia_incidents (AI class); security, privacy, clinical, financial, agriculture, infrastructure, data-integrity and supplier incident workflows are absent. No tested rollback path: root drizzle/ contains 28 up migrations and 0 down migrations.
evidence.risk: A production incident has no defined procedure and a bad migration has no rollback.

evidence.claim: Governance authority tables are writable by the application's own database role, with no RLS, no trigger and no test.
evidence.artifact: privilege probe as beyu_runtime (each statement inside BEGIN..ROLLBACK)
evidence.test: set -a; . ./.env; node -e "...UPDATE governance_capability_registry SET capability_code=capability_code WHERE true" as DATABASE_URL role
evidence.result: UPDATE governance_capability_registry ALLOWED (60 rows); UPDATE users ALLOWED (9); UPDATE role_assignments ALLOWED (9); UPDATE os_registry ALLOWED (9); DELETE governance_decision_registry ALLOWED. A real flip of CAP_POSTING to ACTIVATED returned rowCount=1 and was then restored; registry re-verified at 60/60 LOCKED. Those tables have relrowsecurity=false and 0 triggers; the only 9 user triggers in the schema are on audit_log(2), enterprise_events(2), journal_entries(2), journal_lines(3). Root cause path: scripts/setup-db-role.ts:109 grants select/insert/update/delete on all tables in schema public, and :116 extends it to future tables via ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES. By contrast a direct DELETE FROM audit_log as the same role affects 0 rows under RLS.
evidence.risk: Anything able to issue SQL as the runtime role (leaked DSN, exfiltrating dependency, future injection) can activate all 60 governed capabilities or add a role assignment silently, with no audit row, because audit writes happen only in application code.
evidence.classification: P1. Not P0: no HTTP path executes attacker-controlled SQL (0 sql.raw; all 17 db.execute sites static templates with bound params; 0 SECURITY DEFINER functions of 197 routines).

evidence.claim: Concurrency and basic load behaviour are certified by an existing suite, so performance is partially evidenced rather than entirely unmeasured.
evidence.test: npx vitest run tests/certification/scale-concurrency.test.ts   (BEYU_TEST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3100 set, so the harness hard-fails instead of skipping)
evidence.result: 3/3 pass in 7.6s: 1000 health requests at c=200 all returned 200 with audit+event chains still verifiable (duplicateParents 0, head matched); 120 concurrent login requests all returned 401 with no 5xx, no deadlock and no connection exhaustion; 250 concurrent recordAudit calls produced a fork-free chain.
evidence.risk: This is not production-scale capacity: 2 vCPU sandbox, seeded dataset of 9 users, no p95/p99 percentile reporting, no bulk or report-generation load.

not_verified: Production schema state and drift on the Supabase instance (no admin DSN; owner-controlled).
Production endpoint availability, latency and health (sandbox egress to *.vercel.app failed; no claim made).
Branch protection and required status checks on main (API returned 403 for the available integration).
Managed PostgreSQL PITR, backup retention, storage configuration and measured RPO/RTO.
Real-user and device behaviour: no mobile device, no browser E2E, no wearable, no clinic hardware.
Load, concurrency and capacity at production scale.
Any external assurance activity: no assessor engagement exists in the repository.
Mobile behaviour: no device, emulator or browser E2E was available in this environment, so the Flutter client is NOT_VERIFIED rather than verified.
Whether GitHub branch protection and required checks are configured (the API returns 403 for the available integration).
external_constraints: No production credentials, no cloud infrastructure and no external assurance programme were created or assumed by this program.
Production database secrets are owner-controlled; CI fails closed rather than inventing a target.
CAP_POSTING and the remaining 59 governed capabilities stay LOCKED until named governance blockers are resolved; activation is a human decision and was not taken to make a report green.
